text:
sara: noticing a p99 spike on the 10g region, looks correlated with a small subset of requests hitting a kernel path misroute. KV cache miss rate jumped ~4x at the same time. any quick ideas?
jon: seeing it too. flameprof shows long tail in kernel selection loop, looks like we keep falling back to a slow matmul kernel after cache eviction.
miguel: is this the hotkey pattern we saw last month? same tenant?
sara: different tenant but similar input distribution (many short prompts followed by long completions). tenant id: T-8421 if you want to filter.
incident-bot: Incident created: infra-perf-p99-1983456789 — Sev-2 latency spike on eng-runtime in 10g. Pager duty notified.
misha: jumping in. I grabbed a short perf trace. key things: adaptive batching shrank due to per-request shape variance; kernel selector used heuristic: prefer quantized kernel unless seq_len>128. For some requests seq_len oscillated so we kept switching kernels which caused cache churn.
elaine: can we flip the kernel_selector feature flag for that region to force stable kernel selection while we investigate?
jon: yes, feature flag exists: `kernel_stable_mode` for region 10g. we can enable for T-8421 only. that should stop the oscillation.
miguel: also recommend pinning `kv_prefix_cache` to 60s for the affected allocation to reduce misses temporarily.
ops-oncall: doing the FF rollout now -> `rbac toggle kernel_stable_mode --region 10g --tenant T-8421`
ops-oncall: done, rolling to 5% -> 50% -> 100% over 90s, monitoring p95/p99.
sara: after 100% rollout, p99 dropped ~35%, KV miss rate down to baseline. graph: `//perf/10g/T-8421/p99` shows clear improvement.
misha: good. next step: collect full traces for a longer window to understand why seq_len oscillates — batching heuristics + client behavior?
jon: I captured a 3-min trace and posted the snippet: ```
[trace] kernel_choice: quantized -> fallback_matmul -> quantized -> fallback_matmul
metrics: kv_miss=0.18 -> 0.63 -> 0.21 -> 0.66
queue_time_ms: 0.6 -> 1.8 -> 0.7 -> 2.0
```
sara: interesting that queue_time spikes align with fallback_matmul events. sounds like expensive kernel selection path holds scheduler lock long enough to block batching.
miguel: theory: when cache misses are high, evictions increase and kernel hint eviction runs more often. eviction job uses the same mempool lock as kernel selector. We should decouple or add try-lock path.
elaine: short-term playbook: 1) FF kernel_stable_mode for affected tenant (done), 2) increase `kv_prefix_cache` TTL (miguel suggested), 3) temporarily lower `batch_aggregation_window_ms` in region 10g to reduce shape variance.
ops-oncall: applying TTL now: `config set kv_prefix_cache.ttl 60 --tenant T-8421 --region 10g` -> applied. lowering batch window to 5ms for region 10g -> applied.
misha: can you also capture `perf_event` for the kernel selection hot loop for the next 20 minutes? add `--sample=1ms` so we get enough resolution.
ops-oncall: started perf sampling.
jon: one more: add a runtime guard so kernel selector will skip fallback if the last kernel switch was <200ms ago. cheap fix and reduces thrash. I can PR.
sara: please do, and add unit test for the guard. after that we can revert feature flag and monitor.
miguel: long-term: separate eviction jobs and kernel selector critical sections; maybe use RCU for KV cache metadata.
incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied — kernel_stable_mode FF + kv TTL + batching tweak. Monitoring for 30m.
sara: recording postmortem notes here: cause = rapid kernel switching + KV cache thrash causing scheduler hold and batching breaks. mitigation = FF + config tweaks. follow-ups: PR for selector guard (jon), decouple eviction lock (miguel), longer perf traces + regression alert.
elaine: I'll draft the incident summary for all-hands and link traces.
jon: PR opened: `runtime: add kernel switch cooldown` -> review pinged.
misha: leaving perf collection running for another 10m, will upload traces to `/perf/artifacts/1983456789`.
ops-oncall: closing out rollout monitors, p99 stable for 25m.
sara: thanks team :thumbsup: open follow-ups in GH and assign owners.
